- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.7) or shows recent reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast to align with sentiment shift.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish; cap forecast at 10-15% above peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 day pullback after spike), model often fails to correct; adjust forecast downward by 2-5% of recent peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates when sentiment is mixed or trending neutral; add 1-3% buffer to forecast if sentiment is 0.0–0.5.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive negative signals, model tends to ignore downward momentum; increase downward bias by 1-2% of recent range.
